definitions.name: Absorbing versus reinjected forward equation
definitions.statement: Full density satisfies ∂t ptilde=L ptilde−λ ptilde+J(λ ptilde); killed interjump density h satisfies ∂t h=(L−λ)h. L is the one-dimensional Fokker–Planck operator −∂x(A·)+∂xx(D·), λ is state-dependent and time-independent in the analyzed formulae, J pushes pre-jump mass to post-jump states.

definitions.name: Pre-jump location law and integrated occupation
definitions.statement: In a valid construction set ui(x)=∫0∞hi(x,t)dt and pi(x)=λ(x)ui(x). The operator J is then applied to pi before starting the next killed interval. This correct operational definition avoids assigning 0/0 at λ=0.
definitions.status: corrected operational definition independently derived; original Eq5 writes ui=pi/λ

theorem_cards.label: Theorem1: first intensity-killing time and pre-jump location
assumptions: Original scope: one-dimensional diffusion with forward L, nonnegative state hazard λ, sufficiently regular solution, zero boundary flux at ±∞, no explosion; exact regularity/nonexplosion criteria are delegated to reference[2].

To use these as probability densities rather than defective subdensities additionally establish P(τ<∞)=1; to move L through a time integral establish the needed domain/integrability and boundary conditions. Source does not spell out these assumptions.
theorem_cards.statement: p_location(x)=∫0∞λ(x)h(x,t)dt and p_time(t)=∫Rλ(x)h(x,t)dx. With no killing by another mechanism their total mass is P(τ<∞), which may be below1.
proof_steps: Integrate killed forward equation spatially, use conservation of L to obtain −s′(t)=∫λh.
The absorbed component has no spatial transport, so integrate ∂tq=λh over time.

theorem_cards.label: Theorems2–3: sequential resolvent map
assumptions: Start first interval from known p0; restart later interval from Jpi−1 where J must be a mass-preserving pushforward on the chosen state space.
Killed semigroup has an integrable potential on the starting class and T=λ−L admits the required positive inverse; no-explosion alone is insufficient.
All state/time integrals and L/time-integral interchange need a valid Fubini/domain argument; fixed point and convergence are explicitly assumed or treated heuristically.
theorem_cards.statement: The coherent indexing is hi(0)=Jpi−1 for i>1 (h1(0)=p0), pi=∫λhi, ui=∫hi. Then Tui+1=J(λui), ui+1=T−1J(λui). Eq4 as printed labels the integrated hi output pi+1 while calling hi the ith interval; that indexing is not used literally.
proof_steps: Integrate ∂thi=(L−λ)hi from0 to∞ with terminal limit zero: −hi(0)=(L−λ)ui.
Thus Tui=hi(0), and restarting gives the displayed resolvent map.
Use occupation ui as primary unknown; λui is jump law and a positive ui on a zero-hazard region is possible.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem4/Corollary1: stationary intensity bias
assumptions: Source assumes a fixed point ustar exists and compares stationary nullspaces without a stated uniqueness hypothesis.

Valid transfer requires an invariant time law π, a finite positive mean hazard ∫λdπ and a compatible stationary embedded jump law; identifying any nullvector with π requires uniqueness or matching ergodic class.
theorem_cards.statement: Source states (L−λ+Jλ)ustar=0, pstar=λustar and claims pstar equals full stationary law iff λ is constant. Operational intensity-bias relation is pstar(dx)=λ(x)π(dx)/∫λdπ; equality requires λ constant π-almost everywhere, rather than globally.
proof_steps: The two stationary equations have the same operator.
Normalize time law by ∫π=1 and event law by ∫λustar=1.
Equality of the two normalized measures constrains λ only on the support of π; the printed proof does not establish a unique nullspace.
theorem_cards.proof_verification: Formal stationary equation read; global iff narrowed to supported law and missing uniqueness recorded.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem5 and AppendixA: interjump moments
assumptions: Integrable killed occupation yields finite first moment; for kth moment justify corresponding weighted time integrals, integration by parts and vanishing endpoint terms.
If λ has zeros, compute using occupation rather than pi/λ.
theorem_cards.statement: Eτi=∫ui under finite expectation. For T=λ−L, vi=T−1ui=∫0∞t hi(t)dt, so Eτi²=2∫vi; the printed AppendixA states −∫vi and is false even for constant hazard. Higher moments require the repeated resolvent hierarchy and their own integrability.
proof_steps: Eτ=∫0∞P(τ>t)dt=∫ui by Tonelli for nonnegative h.
Eτ²=2∫0∞tP(τ>t)dt. Integrating t times the killed equation gives Tvi=ui.
For L=0, λ=c>0, normalized p0 gives u=p0/c, v=p0/c², actual Eτ²=2/c², whereas the printed formula gives −1/c².
